title: Requests
body: Each page view, image download or order is a request. There are three kinds in the game. Files (images, scripts) are cheap to serve from storage. Reads (viewing a page) need a server and usually a database. Orders (writes) must be saved safely, so they need a real database.

title: Load and capacity
body: Every component can do a fixed amount of work per second: its capacity. Load is how much of that it's using. Under 80% it's green and fast. Between 80% and 100% it turns amber and slows down. Above 100% it turns red and starts dropping requests. Fix it with a bigger size, more copies, or by taking work away from it.

title: Latency (p95)
body: Latency is the time a request takes, in milliseconds. The game reports p95: 95% of requests were faster than this number. It shows the slow experiences that an average would hide. Every hop between components adds a little, and overloaded components add a lot.

title: Availability
summary: The share of requests that worked.
body: If 1,000 customers click and 999 succeed, availability is 99.9%. It sounds high, but 99% still means 1 in 100 customers saw an error. Crashes, overloads and broken connections all lower it.

title: Single point of failure
summary: One part that takes everything down.
body: Any component whose failure stops the whole site is a single point of failure, like a lone web server. Remove it with redundancy: two or more copies behind a load balancer, so one can fail while the others carry on.

title: Availability Zones
summary: Separate data centres in one region.
body: An AWS region (say, London) is made of several Availability Zones: separate data centres with their own power and network. Spreading servers across two zones means a problem in one doesn't take you offline.

title: Cost per month
summary: What your design costs to run.
body: Each component has a monthly price, and some also charge per request. The game shows what your design would cost if every day looked like this one. Each level has a budget. Coming in well under it scores bonus points, and going over fails the level.
